clinician.trajectory_summary: A 10-day-old newborn, delivered via elective C-section with APGAR 8/9, presented with severe respiratory distress manifesting a few hours after birth, requiring mechanical ventilation and antibiotic treatment. Concurrent with the respiratory presentation, the infant exhibited reduced mobility in the left lower limb. Initial imaging (chest X-ray and abdominal ultrasound) were normal; echocardiography showed a patent foramen ovale with mild shunt. The respiratory distress was diagnosed as acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and resolved after approximately 48 hours of supportive therapy. Subsequent skeletal imaging revealed the underlying osteodysplastic pathology: X-ray identified a mid-diaphyseal tibial fracture; CT scan demonstrated morphostructural alteration of the left tibia with curvature in the distal diaphyseal segment, discontinuities in the bone cortex with cortical thickening, multiple irregularly distributed hypodense areas, and a curved fibula with hypodensity in the proximal diaphyseal region. Genetic counseling ruled out neurofibromatosis type 1 phenotypic features. The imaging findings and clinical presentation were consistent with congenital tibial pseudarthrosis, an osteodysplastic condition characterized by bone dysplasia, cortical discontinuity, and abnormal bone quality, occurring in the absence of trauma history.
